passage: This offer does not create a contract of employment for any specific duration. You will be free to resign your position whenever you choose, for any reason or no reason, and the Company retains the same right to end the relationship on similar terms, with no obligation to state a reason or provide advance warning.

As a condition of employment, you and the Company agree that any claim arising out of or relating to your employment will be resolved through final, binding arbitration on an individual basis rather than through a lawsuit or jury trial. Neither party may bring or join a class, collective, or representative proceeding against the other, and this requirement extends even to disputes about whether this provision itself can be enforced.

Before extending a final offer, we may request a background screening report prepared by a third-party consumer reporting agency, which could include verification of prior employment, education, and criminal history. This notice is provided to you as a standalone document, separate from any release or other paperwork, because applicable law requires that the disclosure not be combined with other agreements.

Any medical information gathered as part of a post-offer physical will be stored separately from your general personnel file and accessed only on a need-to-know basis. Supervisors may be told only what accommodations or work restrictions apply, safety staff may be alerted if emergency treatment could become necessary, and the records may otherwise be shared only with government auditors verifying compliance.

Hourly employees must obtain manager sign-off before working beyond their scheduled hours. That said, the Company will still compensate overtime it was aware of, or reasonably should have been aware of, even when prior approval was skipped, though it has no duty to pay for hours it never had any way of learning about.

The restrictive covenant in Section 9 may or may not be enforceable depending on which state's law applies to you. A number of jurisdictions refuse to enforce this type of restraint on trade altogether, allowing it only in narrow circumstances such as the sale of a company, while other states will enforce it so long as the scope is reasonable, does not unduly burden the employee, and does not harm the public interest.

The parties may agree between themselves on a broad definition of what qualifies as proprietary information under this Agreement. However, to the extent either side later seeks trade-secret protection under statute rather than relying on contract alone, only information that is genuinely kept secret through reasonable efforts and that derives value from not being publicly known will qualify, regardless of how broadly this Agreement's own confidentiality definition is written.

Inventor agrees that, effective immediately upon creation of any Invention, all right, title, and interest therein shall automatically vest in and be deemed assigned to the Company, without need for any further instrument. The parties intend this present-tense assignment language to operate differently from a mere promise to assign in the future, so that ownership transfers the moment the invention is conceived rather than waiting on a later signed document.

By clicking the "I Accept" button below, you acknowledge that you have read and agree to be bound by this License. Courts have generally enforced online agreements of this type where the user must take some affirmative step to signal agreement, in contrast to terms that are merely posted via a link with no required action, which are enforced only if the user had actual or reasonably inferable notice of them.

In connection with Seller's sale of all of the goodwill and operating assets of the Business to Buyer, Seller agrees not to engage in a competing enterprise within the Territory for so long as Buyer, or any successor who acquires the goodwill from Buyer, continues to operate a similar business there. The parties acknowledge that such a restriction, tied to the sale of a business's goodwill, falls within a recognized exception to the general policy against restraints on trade.

Because the Company will come into possession of employees' medical information in connection with this program, it agrees to adopt and maintain reasonable administrative safeguards designed to prevent that information from being accessed, used, or disclosed by anyone without proper authorization.

Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, a confidentiality or nondisparagement obligation signed before a claim arises -- such as the one contained in an employment contract entered into at the start of the relationship -- is not enforceable to silence a party from later discussing a dispute involving alleged sexual harassment or sexual assault that is said to violate law.

Tenant shall pay Landlord a security deposit equal to one month's rent at signing. Landlord may apply this deposit only toward unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear and tear, cleaning required to restore the unit to its condition at move-in, and any future failure by Tenant to return property as agreed, and must send Tenant a written accounting of any deductions, along with the balance, within three weeks after the tenancy ends.

Before vacating, Tenant has the right to ask Landlord to walk through the unit in advance so Tenant can address any issues before the final deposit accounting. If Tenant makes that request, Landlord must give at least two days' written notice of the scheduled time and may not conduct the walkthrough more than fourteen days ahead of the actual move-out date.

Landlord warrants that the Premises, throughout the tenancy, will have intact weatherproofing, functioning plumbing and gas lines meeting the applicable building code, hot and cold running water tied into an approved sewer system, operable heating and electrical systems, and common areas kept free of trash, pests, and rodents, along with floors and stairways maintained in safe condition.

Unless this transaction falls within a recognized exemption -- such as a court-ordered sale, a transfer by a trustee administering an estate (where the trustee isn't a prior owner or recent occupant), a transfer between co-owners or close relatives, or a transfer to a government entity -- Seller must deliver a completed statutory disclosure form to Buyer before closing, and the parties acknowledge that this obligation cannot be waived by agreement.

If Tenant pays the full amount demanded in this notice within the three-day period stated above, the default is cured and the tenancy continues as though no notice had ever been given. Tenant's timely payment of the exact sum owed, within the window provided, prevents Landlord from proceeding on a nonpayment theory in any subsequent unlawful detainer action.

This Sublease creates obligations running between Sublessor and Subtenant only. Subtenant has no direct contractual relationship with Master Landlord by virtue of this arrangement, may not enforce the Master Lease directly against Master Landlord, and Master Landlord likewise has no right to collect rent or pursue remedies directly against Subtenant, except as the Master Lease, Master Landlord's written consent, or a separate tri-party agreement may otherwise provide.

I declare that I am of sound mind, understand that I am executing my Last Will and Testament, am aware of the nature and extent of the property I own, and recognize the natural objects of my bounty, including my family members. I further acknowledge that this Will would not be valid if my distribution choices were the product of delusions caused by a mental disorder, rather than my genuine wishes.

This Will must be signed by me, or by another person in my presence and at my direction, and must be witnessed by no fewer than two individuals who are both present at the same time, who observe me sign or acknowledge my signature, and who understand that the document they are witnessing is my Will.

Separate from a formally witnessed will, state law also recognizes a will written and signed entirely in the testator's own hand, with no witnesses required at all. Leaving such a document undated is risky, however: if there is any doubt about which of two competing documents controls, or whether the testator had capacity when it was written, an undated handwritten will can be defeated unless its timing can otherwise be established.

In this Will, I nominate [Name] to serve as guardian of my minor child's person and estate. This nomination will only take legal effect if the child's other living parent either joins in or consents to the same person, or, at the time any guardianship petition is actually filed, that other parent has died, been found legally incapable of consenting, or is a parent whose consent would not otherwise be required.

To be valid, this Power of Attorney must state the date it is signed, be executed by the Principal personally (or by another adult acting in the Principal's presence at the Principal's direction), and either be notarized or signed by two qualified witnesses who personally observe the signing or the Principal's acknowledgment of it. The Agent named in this document is not permitted to serve as one of those witnesses.

Unless this document specifically and expressly grants the following powers, my Agent may not: create, amend, revoke, or fund any trust on my behalf; make or revoke gifts of my property; disclaim an inheritance or other interest on my behalf; change beneficiary designations on my accounts or policies; or borrow money from me as Agent. Regardless of what express language this Power of Attorney contains, my Agent may never execute, modify, or revoke my Will.

Unless this instrument states otherwise, the Trust created here remains revocable by the Settlor during the Settlor's lifetime. The Settlor may revoke it, in whole or part, by the method this Trust specifies or, if none is specified as the only permitted method, by delivering a signed writing -- other than a Will -- to the Trustee while the Settlor is still living.

The parties intend this Agreement to constitute a premarital contract, entered into in anticipation of their upcoming marriage and intended to take effect upon the solemnization of that marriage. Should the parties never actually marry, this Agreement will have no force or effect whatsoever.

Any waiver of spousal support contained in this Agreement is enforceable against a party only if that party was represented by their own independent attorney when the Agreement was signed, and only if the waiver is not unconscionable at the time either party later tries to enforce it. Having had independent counsel at signing does not, by itself, guarantee that an otherwise-unconscionable waiver will be upheld.

Nothing in this Agreement limits, waives, or otherwise affects either party's child support obligations or a child's right to receive support, regardless of any other terms the parties have agreed to here.

The parties recognize that California law generally requires their community estate to be divided equally between them unless they otherwise agree in writing or stipulate orally before the court. By entering into this settlement, which allocates certain community assets unequally in value, the parties are exercising that statutory right to agree to a different division.

In setting the amount and duration of spousal support, the parties acknowledge the court must weigh factors including each spouse's marketable skills and job prospects, any career sacrifices made to raise children or run the household, contributions one spouse made to the other's education or career, the paying spouse's actual ability to pay, each party's needs measured against their marital standard of living, the length of the marriage, and any documented history of domestic violence, among other relevant circumstances.

In deciding custody, the court will look first to the child's health, safety, and overall welfare, and will also weigh any history of abuse by either parent, how much ongoing contact the child has with each parent, and any pattern of habitual drug or alcohol abuse by either parent. The court will not take into account either parent's sexual orientation or gender identity in making this determination.

The Articles of Organization filed with the Secretary of State must set out the LLC's stated purpose, its legal name in compliance with the naming rules for limited liability companies, the street address of its principal office (plus a mailing address if different), and the name and address of its initial agent for service of process. If the Articles are silent on management structure, the LLC defaults by law to being managed by its members rather than by one or more designated managers.

The fiduciary obligations owed within the Company depend on how it is managed. In a member-managed structure, every member owes the others a duty of loyalty -- including turning over any profit taken from a company opportunity -- plus a duty of care that is breached only by gross negligence, recklessness, or knowing illegality. If the Company is instead manager-managed, those same duties shift to the managers, and an ordinary member who isn't also a manager owes the company no fiduciary duty purely by virtue of holding membership interests.

The Corporation may indemnify any officer, director, or other agent named as a party to litigation because of their role with the Corporation, covering reasonably incurred expenses, settlements, judgments, and fines, provided that person acted honestly and in a manner they reasonably believed served the Corporation's best interests -- and, in any criminal matter, had no reason to believe their conduct was unlawful.

A transfer restriction on membership interests binds only the parties who agreed to it unless it is actually set out in the Company's operating agreement itself, rather than in a separate side letter. A transfer that violates a restriction written into the operating agreement has no effect against anyone who knew about the restriction when the transfer took place, and the Company need not recognize a transferee's rights until it receives actual notice that a transfer has occurred.

Unless this Agreement provides otherwise, every Partner of the Partnership has an equal voice in managing and conducting partnership business, irrespective of how much capital any individual Partner has contributed, how much time they devote to the enterprise, or what particular role they play.

A partner's withdrawal from the Partnership does not, standing alone, dissolve it; dissolution occurs only upon specific triggering events. Where the Partnership has no fixed term, winding up requires the express agreement of at least half the remaining partners, including any partner who withdrew improperly within the prior ninety days; where a definite term or undertaking exists, dissolution instead follows from a majority-in-interest's refusal to continue after certain withdrawals, a unanimous vote to wind up, or the term's expiration.

When an employee requests a reasonable accommodation, the Company commits to engaging in a good-faith, interactive process to identify one that works. The Company can be held liable for failing to do so in good faith, but generally only if a workable accommodation actually existed and the breakdown in the process -- not some other cause -- is what kept it from being put in place.

The Company will promptly look into any harassment complaint and take whatever corrective steps the findings warrant. Doing so is more than a best practice: under federal law, an employer can only assert certain defenses to a harassment claim if it shows it took reasonable steps to prevent and correct the conduct and that the complaining employee unreasonably failed to use the available reporting channels.

Qualified employees may take up to twelve weeks of leave within a rolling twelve-month window for the birth or adoption of a child, to care for a seriously ill spouse, parent, or child, or because of their own serious health condition that prevents them from doing their job.

No agreement, policy, or condition of employment -- including any arbitration clause signed before a dispute arises -- can require an employee to give up the whistleblower protections described above. To the extent an arbitration agreement purports to force this type of claim into arbitration, it is unenforceable as to that claim.

An employee who works more than five hours in a shift must be given an unpaid meal break of at least half an hour, unless the total shift is six hours or less and both the employee and the Company agree to skip it. Employees working more than ten hours must receive a second half-hour break, which can likewise be waived by mutual agreement if the full shift doesn't exceed twelve hours and the first break wasn't already waived.

In addition to meal breaks, the Company must give employees paid rest breaks, ideally near the midpoint of each work segment, calculated at ten minutes for every four hours worked or major fraction thereof. No rest break is required for a shift under three and a half hours, and any rest break actually provided counts as paid working time with no corresponding wage deduction.

The Company will reimburse an employee for reasonable out-of-pocket costs necessarily incurred while carrying out assigned duties or following a supervisor's instructions, including instructions later deemed improper, unless the employee knew at the time that what was being asked was unlawful.

If you participate in the Company's group health plan, your separation will typically count as a qualifying event entitling you to continue that same coverage, at your own expense, for up to eighteen months under federal law, unless your termination resulted from gross misconduct. The Company will promptly notify the plan administrator of your departure so the formal notice of your continuation rights can be sent to you.

Because Employee is over forty, this release of age-discrimination claims will only be valid if it is written in plain English, specifically identifies the age-discrimination rights being released, does not attempt to cover any future claims, is supported by consideration beyond what Employee is already entitled to receive, advises Employee in writing to speak with a lawyer first, and gives Employee no fewer than twenty-one days to decide -- or forty-five days if this release is part of a broader layoff -- along with a week afterward to revoke the signature.

A commission does not automatically become an earned wage the moment the underlying sale closes; the Company may lawfully tie final entitlement to an additional condition, such as the customer's payment actually being received, and until that condition is satisfied, any amount paid out beforehand is treated as a draw against future commissions rather than wages actually owed.

Continuation coverage rights can be triggered by any of several listed events: the covered worker's death, a termination of employment other than for gross misconduct or a cut in hours, a divorce or legal separation from the covered worker, the covered worker becoming eligible for Medicare, a dependent child aging out of eligibility under the plan, or specific bankruptcy proceedings affecting retiree health coverage.

Once we are properly served with a court-issued earnings withholding order directing us to garnish an employee's wages, we are legally required to comply, and in situations where multiple withholding orders arrive for the same employee, we generally honor whichever order was served on us first, subject to separate priority rules that apply to support and tax-related orders.

During the initial sixty-day transition period after a change in contractors, a retained worker may be discharged only for reasons tied to that individual's own job performance or conduct. At the end of the sixty days, the new contractor must prepare a written performance review for each retained worker and must offer continued employment to anyone whose performance was satisfactory; after that point, the job reverts to ordinary at-will status.

This Agreement, together with any exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire understanding between the parties regarding its subject matter and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral. No modification of this Agreement will be effective unless made in writing and signed by both parties.

Neither party shall be liable for any failure or delay in performance under this Agreement to the extent such failure or delay is caused by circumstances beyond its reasonable control, including but not limited to natural disasters, war, labor disputes, or governmental action, provided that the affected party gives prompt notice and uses reasonable efforts to resume performance as soon as practicable.

Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this international supply agreement shall be referred to and finally resolved by arbitration administered by the International Chamber of Commerce in Geneva, Switzerland, with the arbitral tribunal applying the substantive law of Switzerland, and the parties waive any right to resolve such disputes in the national courts of either party's home jurisdiction.

Upon each secondary sale of the digital collectible on a supported marketplace, the smart contract will automatically remit a five percent royalty to the original creator's connected wallet address, and the creator retains no right to modify this royalty percentage once the collection has been minted onto the blockchain.

If the Contractor fails to achieve Substantial Completion of the Project by the date specified in the Construction Schedule, Contractor shall pay Owner liquidated damages in the amount of two thousand dollars for each calendar day of delay thereafter, not as a penalty but as a reasonable pre-estimate of Owner's anticipated losses from the delay.
